On the homological conjectures for Artin algebras

Haruhisa Enomoto Address: Haruhisa Enomoto: Parakeet Inc., Japan Email address: haruhisa.enomoto.math@gmail.com and Rene Marczinzik Address: Rene Marczinzik: Mathematical Institute of the University of Bonn, Endenicher Allee 60, 53115 Bonn, Germany Email address: marczire@math.uni-bonn.de
Date: September 24, 2026
Abstract.

We prove that the Auslander–Reiten conjecture, the generalised Nakayama conjecture, the Nakayama conjecture, and each of the two Tachikawa conjectures are globally equivalent for Artin algebras over any fixed commutative artinian ring. For finite dimensional algebras over a fixed field, we also prove that the derived invariance of the Nakayama conjecture is equivalent to the truth of the Nakayama conjecture for all such algebras, answering a question raised by Chen and Xi.

Key words and phrases: 
Tachikawa conjectures, Auslander–Reiten conjecture, Nakayama conjecture, dominant dimension, trivial extensions, Morita algebras, derived equivalences
2020 Mathematics Subject Classification
Primary 16E10; Secondary 16D50, 16E30, 16G10

1. Introduction

In this article we give a new viewpoint on the longstanding homological conjectures for Artin algebras. For background and historical accounts, see the surveys of Happel [Hap91], Yamagata [Yam96], and Huisgen-Zimmermann [HZ95].

Throughout the first three sections, RR is a fixed commutative artinian ring, algebras are Artin RR-algebras, and modules are finitely generated right modules. The finitistic dimension of AA is

findimA=sup{pdimAM∣M∈modA,pdimAM<∞}.\operatorname{findim}A=\sup\{\pdim_{A}M\mid M\in\operatorname{mod}A,\ \pdim_{A}M<\infty\}.

For an algebra AA with minimal injective coresolution

0⟶AA⟶I0⟶I1⟶⋯,0\longrightarrow A_{A}\longrightarrow I^{0}\longrightarrow I^{1}\longrightarrow\cdots,

the dominant dimension domdim⁡A\domdim A is the least n≥0n\geq 0 such that InI^{n} is not projective, and is infinite if all the terms are projective. In particular, a selfinjective algebra has infinite dominant dimension. The grade of a module MM is

gradeA⁡M=inf{i≥0∣ExtAi⁡(M,A)≠0},inf∅=∞.\operatorname{grade}_{A}M=\inf\{i\geq 0\mid\Ext_{A}^{i}(M,A)\neq 0\},\qquad\inf\varnothing=\infty.

Following Gélinas [Gel22, Definition 1.1], the depth of AA is the supremum of the grades of its simple right modules. Since there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of simple modules, this depth is finite exactly when each simple module has finite grade.

We next recall the four most important homological conjectures related to finiteness of homological dimensions for Artin algebras. The numbers in parentheses refer to the list of homological conjectures in [ARS95, p. 410].

  1. (1)

    The finitistic dimension conjecture (FDC): every Artin algebra has finite finitistic dimension (Conjecture (11)).

  2. (2)

    The Gorenstein symmetry conjecture (GSC): the left regular module of an Artin algebra has finite injective dimension if and only if the right regular module does (Conjecture (13)).

  3. (3)

    The generalised Nakayama conjecture (GNC): every Artin algebra has finite depth (Conjecture (9)).

  4. (4)

    The Nakayama conjecture (NC): every non-selfinjective Artin algebra has finite dominant dimension (Conjecture (8)).

Many of those conjectures are quite old. For example the Nakayama conjecture dates back to the 1950’s, see [Nak58]. The following four further prominent conjectures will be relevant:

  1. (1)

    The strong Nakayama conjecture (SNC): every nonzero module has finite grade (Conjecture (12) in [ARS95]).

  2. (2)

    The Auslander–Reiten conjecture (ARC): if ExtAi⁡(M,M⊕A)=0\Ext_{A}^{i}(M,M\oplus A)=0 for every i>0i>0, then MM is projective (Conjecture (10) in [ARS95]).

  3. (3)

    The first Tachikawa conjecture (TC1): if ExtAi⁡(D​A,A)=0\Ext_{A}^{i}(DA,A)=0 for every i>0i>0, then AA is selfinjective [Tac73, §8].

  4. (4)

    The second Tachikawa conjecture (TC2): if AA is selfinjective and ExtAi⁡(M,M)=0\Ext_{A}^{i}(M,M)=0 for every i>0i>0, then MM is projective [Tac73, §8].

An implication or equivalence between conjectures is called global if it concerns their validity for all Artin RR-algebras over the fixed ring RR; TC2 is quantified over the selfinjective ones. We remark, that global equivalence need not be an equivalence for each individual algebra. For example, NC holds for every local Artin algebra, but the corresponding Tachikawa questions remain open in general even for commutative artinian local rings. For recent examples concerning low-degree Ext vanishing in that setting, see [BM26]. For related open conjectures over commutative local rings inspired by the conjectures in the Artin algebra case, see for example [ABS05] and [HL04].

Auslander and Reiten proved the global equivalence of ARC and GNC [AR75]. Classical results also give the global equivalence of NC with the conjunction of TC1 and TC2; see [Mue68, Tac73]. The following familiar implications provide the context for our results; see [ARS95, p. 410] and [Yam96, §3.4]:

All arrows in this diagram are global implications.

Our first main result shows that each Tachikawa conjecture separately implies ARC.

Theorem 1.1.

Fix a commutative artinian ring RR. The following conjectures are globally equivalent for Artin RR-algebras:

  1. (1)

    the Auslander–Reiten conjecture;

  2. (2)

    the generalised Nakayama conjecture;

  3. (3)

    the Nakayama conjecture;

  4. (4)

    the first Tachikawa conjecture;

  5. (5)

    the second Tachikawa conjecture.

We will prove this theorem using constructions related to rr-fold trivial extension algebras to show that the first Tachikawa conjecture implies the Auslander-Reiten conjecture globally and then also to show that the second Tachikawa conjecture implies the Auslander-Reiten conjecture globally. Having proved this, the above diagram looks as follows and proves theorem 1.1:

Thus we can simplify it to the following diagram, where up to global equivalence only 4 homological conjectures remain:

Here NC represents any of the five globally equivalent conjectures in Theorem 1.1, we picked the Nakayama conjecture as a representative as it might be the historically most important one.

Our second application concerns finite dimensional algebras over a fixed field KK. Chen and Xi formulated the following conjecture [CX16, §5.2, conjecture (1)]; see also [Xi18, Conjecture 6.5].

Conjecture 1.2 (Chen–Xi).

If AA and BB are derived equivalent finite dimensional KK-algebras, then domdim⁡A<∞\domdim A<\infty if and only if domdim⁡B<∞\domdim B<\infty.

Write NC⁡(A)\mathrm{NC}(A) for the implication that domdim⁡A=∞\domdim A=\infty forces AA to be selfinjective.

Theorem 1.3.

For finite dimensional algebras over a fixed field KK, the following are equivalent:

  1. (1)

    NC holds for every such algebra;

  2. (2)

    NC⁡(A)\mathrm{NC}(A) and NC⁡(B)\mathrm{NC}(B) are equivalent whenever AA and BB are derived equivalent;

  3. (3)

    the Chen–Xi conjecture holds.

2. Preliminaries

RR is a fixed commutative artinian ring, EE is an injective envelope of R/rad⁡RR/\rad R, and D=HomR⁡(−,E)D=\Hom_{R}(-,E). An algebra means an associative unital Artin RR-algebra, finite as an RR-module. All modules are finitely generated right modules unless otherwise stated. We write mod⁡A\operatorname{mod}A for the module category of finitely generated AA-modules and add⁡M\add M for the full subcategory of direct summands of finite direct sums of copies of MM for an AA-module MM. We refer to [ASS06, SY11, ARS95] for standard textbooks on representation theory of Artin algebras. The Nakayama functor is given by

νA=DHomA(−,A)≅−⊗ADA.\nu_{A}=D\Hom_{A}(-,A)\cong-\otimes_{A}DA.

A module MM is selforthogonal if ExtAi⁡(M,M)=0\Ext_{A}^{i}(M,M)=0 for every i>0i>0 and an algebra is selfinjective if its right regular module is injective. A module VV is a generator if A∈add⁡VA\in\add V, and a cogenerator if D​A∈add⁡VDA\in\add V. Thus a generator-cogenerator contains every projective and every injective module in its additive closure. An additive generator of a subcategory 𝒞\mathcal{C} is a module QQ with 𝒞=add⁡Q\mathcal{C}=\add Q. Endomorphism algebras are multiplied by composition: a​b=a∘bab=a\circ b. Thus HomA⁡(V,N)\Hom_{A}(V,N) is a right EndA⁡(V)\End_{A}(V)-module by precomposition, while VV is a left EndA⁡(V)\End_{A}(V)-module by evaluation.

Let Γ\Gamma be an algebra, let e∈Γe\in\Gamma be an idempotent and put A=e​Γ​eA=e\Gamma e. Consider

F=−⊗AeΓ:modA⟶modΓ,H=(−)e:modΓ⟶modA.F=-\otimes_{A}e\Gamma:\operatorname{mod}A\longrightarrow\operatorname{mod}\Gamma,\qquad H=(-)e:\operatorname{mod}\Gamma\longrightarrow\operatorname{mod}A.

Then the following hold.

  1. (1)

    FF is fully faithful and preserves and reflects projective modules.

  2. (2)

    If ToriA⁡(M,e​Γ)=0\Tor_{i}^{A}(M,e\Gamma)=0 for every i>0i>0, then, for every Z∈mod⁡ΓZ\in\operatorname{mod}\Gamma and n≥0n\geq 0, there is a natural isomorphism

    (2.1) ExtΓn⁡(F​M,Z)≅ExtAn⁡(M,Z​e).\Ext_{\Gamma}^{n}(FM,Z)\cong\Ext_{A}^{n}(M,Ze).
Proof.

See [APT92, Lemma 3.1(1),(3) and pp. 678–679] for (1), and [APT92, Theorem 3.2(c) and Proposition 3.7(b)] for (2). ∎

Lemma 2.4.

Let V=S⊕WV=S\oplus W be a generator-cogenerator over an algebra SS, and put B=EndS⁡(V)B=\End_{S}(V). If BB is selfinjective, then VV is injective. If SS and BB are selfinjective, then VV is projective-injective.

Proof.

Let j:V↪Ij:V\hookrightarrow I be an injective envelope. Since VV is a cogenerator, I∈add⁡D​S⊆add⁡VI\in\add DS\subseteq\add V. Applying H=HomS⁡(V,−)H=\Hom_{S}(V,-) gives a monomorphism H⁡(j):B↪H⁡(I)H(j):B\hookrightarrow H(I). As BBB_{B} is injective, this has a retraction r:H⁡(I)→Br:H(I)\to B. Lemma 2.2 gives s:I→Vs:I\to V with H⁡(s)=rH(s)=r. It follows that H⁡(s​j)=1H⁡(V)H(sj)=1_{H(V)}, and faithfulness gives s​j=1Vsj=1_{V}. Thus VV is a direct summand of II and is injective. Over a selfinjective algebra, finitely generated injective and projective modules coincide. ∎

Corollary 2.5.

Let SS be selfinjective, let V=S⊕WV=S\oplus W, and suppose that

ExtSi⁡(V,V)=ExtSi⁡(νS​V,V)=0(i>0).\Ext_{S}^{i}(V,V)=\Ext_{S}^{i}(\nu_{S}V,V)=0\qquad(i>0).

If EndS⁡(V)\End_{S}(V) satisfies (TC1)(\mathrm{TC1}), then VV is projective.

Proof.

Proposition 2.3 and (TC1)(\mathrm{TC1}) make EndS⁡(V)\End_{S}(V) selfinjective. Since SS is selfinjective, VV is a generator-cogenerator. Now apply Lemma 2.4. ∎

3. Proof of the main result

We first introduce rr-fold trivial extension algebras (see for example [CDIM25, Section 2.2] for more information and [Hap88, Chapter 2] for the related repetitive algebra) and give their basic properties and then use them to prove our main result.

Definition 3.1.

Let r≥2r\geq 2. The rr-fold trivial extension of AA is Tr​(A)=Ar⊕(D​A)rT_{r}(A)=A^{r}\oplus(DA)^{r}, with multiplication

(3.1) (ai,φi)i=1r​(bi,ψi)i=1r=(ai​bi,ai​ψi+φi​bi+1)i=1r.(a_{i},\varphi_{i})_{i=1}^{r}(b_{i},\psi_{i})_{i=1}^{r}=\bigl(a_{i}b_{i},\ a_{i}\psi_{i}+\varphi_{i}b_{i+1}\bigr)_{i=1}^{r}.

Indices are read modulo rr. In particular,

(3.2) T2​(A)=(AD​AD​AA),T3​(A)=(AD​A00AD​AD​A0A).T_{2}(A)=\begin{pmatrix}A&DA\\ DA&A\end{pmatrix},\qquad T_{3}(A)=\begin{pmatrix}A&DA&0\\ 0&A&DA\\ DA&0&A\end{pmatrix}.

Products of two off-diagonal entries are defined to be zero.

The matrix notation does not prescribe products of two dual elements; such products are zero by definition.

Put Γ=Tr​(A)\Gamma=T_{r}(A) and let eie_{i} denote the iith diagonal identity. These idempotents are pairwise orthogonal and sum to 11. Every corner ei​Γ​eie_{i}\Gamma e_{i} is identified with the same algebra AA. Tr​(A)T_{r}(A) is an Artin RR-algebra and for a right Γ\Gamma-module ZZ one has the direct sum of RR-modules Z=⨁j=1rZ​ejZ=\bigoplus_{j=1}^{r}Ze_{j}. We call Z​ejZe_{j} its jjth component. Note that multiplication by an element of ei​Γ​ei+1=D​Ae_{i}\Gamma e_{i+1}=DA can send the iith component to the (i+1)(i+1)st. The functor Z↦Z​ejZ\mapsto Ze_{j} is exact, since taking the image of an idempotent preserves exact sequences.

Define an automorphism ρ\rho of Γ\Gamma by

ρ⁡((ai,φi)i)=(ai−1,φi−1)i.\rho((a_{i},\varphi_{i})_{i})=(a_{i-1},\varphi_{i-1})_{i}.

naturally in ZZ.

The dual bimodule action on D​ΓD\Gamma is (a​f​b)​(y)=f​(b​y​a)(afb)(y)=f(bya). Therefore

a​θ​(x)=θ⁡(a​x),θ⁡(x)​b=θ⁡(x​ρ​(b)).a\theta(x)=\theta(ax),\qquad\theta(x)b=\theta(x\rho(b)).

Thus θ\theta identifies D​ΓD\Gamma with Γρ1{}_{1}\Gamma_{\rho}, proving (3.3). Since D​ΓD\Gamma is injective as a right module and twisting by an automorphism is an exact autoequivalence, Γ\Gamma is selfinjective. Finally,

which proves (3.4). ∎

Thus the first summand sits at eie_{i} and the second at ei+1e_{i+1}.

Lemma 3.3.

For every M∈mod⁡AM\in\operatorname{mod}A one has

(3.8) (FiM)ei≅M,(FiM)ei+1≅M⊗ADA,(FiM)ej=0(j∉{i,i+1}).(F_{i}M)e_{i}\cong M,\qquad(F_{i}M)e_{i+1}\cong M\otimes_{A}DA,\qquad(F_{i}M)e_{j}=0\quad(j\notin\{i,i+1\}).

For the Nakayama-functor assertion, Lemma 3.2 gives a natural isomorphism

νΓ​(Fi​M)≅(Fi​M)ρ.\nu_{\Gamma}(F_{i}M)\cong(F_{i}M)_{\rho}.

αM:(Fi​M)ρ→∼Fi−1​M.\alpha_{M}:(F_{i}M)_{\rho}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }F_{i-1}M.

f⊕(f⊗AidD​A).f\oplus(f\otimes_{A}\operatorname{id}_{DA}).

Hence

αM′∘(Fi​f)ρ=Fi−1​f∘αM,\alpha_{M^{\prime}}\circ(F_{i}f)_{\rho}=F_{i-1}f\circ\alpha_{M},

so αM\alpha_{M} is natural in MM. Composing with the natural isomorphism supplied by Lemma 3.2 proves (3.9). ∎

Proposition 3.4.

Suppose M∈mod⁡AM\in\operatorname{mod}A satisfies ExtAj⁡(M,A)=0\Ext_{A}^{j}(M,A)=0 for every j>0j>0. Then for i=1,…,ri=1,\ldots,r, every Z∈mod⁡ΓZ\in\operatorname{mod}\Gamma and every n≥0n\geq 0,

(3.10) ExtΓn⁡(Fi​M,Z)≅ExtAn⁡(M,Z​ei).\Ext_{\Gamma}^{n}(F_{i}M,Z)\cong\Ext_{A}^{n}(M,Ze_{i}).

In particular, if MM is selforthogonal and X=F1​MX=F_{1}M, then ExtΓn⁡(X,X)=0\Ext_{\Gamma}^{n}(X,X)=0 for every n>0n>0. If also r≥3r\geq 3, then

(3.11) ExtΓn⁡(νΓ​X,X)=0(n≥0).\Ext_{\Gamma}^{n}(\nu_{\Gamma}X,X)=0\qquad(n\geq 0).
Proof.

As a left AA-module, ei​Γ≅A⊕D​Ae_{i}\Gamma\cong A\oplus DA. Let P∙→MP_{\bullet}\to M be a projective resolution. Tensor–Hom adjunction and double duality identify the cochain complexes

D⁡(P∙⊗AD​A)≅HomA⁡(P∙,D​D​A)≅HomA⁡(P∙,A).D(P_{\bullet}\otimes_{A}DA)\cong\Hom_{A}(P_{\bullet},DDA)\cong\Hom_{A}(P_{\bullet},A).

The functor DD is exact and faithful, so

D​TorjA⁡(M,D​A)≅ExtAj⁡(M,A)=0(j>0).D\Tor_{j}^{A}(M,DA)\cong\Ext_{A}^{j}(M,A)=0\qquad(j>0).

It follows that TorjA⁡(M,ei​Γ)=0\Tor_{j}^{A}(M,e_{i}\Gamma)=0 for every j>0j>0. Lemma 2.1 proves (3.10).

Now let X=F1​MX=F_{1}M and suppose that MM is selforthogonal. Since X​e1≅MXe_{1}\cong M, equation (3.10) gives

ExtΓn⁡(X,X)≅ExtAn⁡(M,M)=0(n>0).\Ext_{\Gamma}^{n}(X,X)\cong\Ext_{A}^{n}(M,M)=0\qquad(n>0).

Now assume r≥3r\geq 3. Lemma 3.3 gives νΓ​X≅Fr​M\nu_{\Gamma}X\cong F_{r}M. Since rr differs from 11 and 22, we have X​er=0Xe_{r}=0. Thus

ExtΓn⁡(νΓ​X,X)≅ExtΓn⁡(Fr​M,X)≅ExtAn⁡(M,X​er)=0(n≥0).\Ext_{\Gamma}^{n}(\nu_{\Gamma}X,X)\cong\Ext_{\Gamma}^{n}(F_{r}M,X)\cong\Ext_{A}^{n}(M,Xe_{r})=0\qquad(n\geq 0).

This proves (3.11). ∎

We first apply the two-fold extension to the second Tachikawa conjecture.

Theorem 3.5.

Let AA be an Artin RR-algebra. If T2​(A)T_{2}(A) satisfies (TC2)(\mathrm{TC2}), then AA satisfies (ARC)(\mathrm{ARC}). Consequently, global (TC2)(\mathrm{TC2}) implies global (ARC)(\mathrm{ARC}).

Proof.

Let MM satisfy ExtAi⁡(M,M⊕A)=0\Ext_{A}^{i}(M,M\oplus A)=0 for every i>0i>0. Put Γ=T2​(A)\Gamma=T_{2}(A) and X=M⊗Ae1​ΓX=M\otimes_{A}e_{1}\Gamma. The algebra Γ\Gamma is selfinjective by Lemma 3.2. Proposition 3.4 gives

ExtΓi⁡(X,X)≅ExtAi⁡(M,M)=0(i>0).\Ext_{\Gamma}^{i}(X,X)\cong\Ext_{A}^{i}(M,M)=0\qquad(i>0).

Thus (TC2)(\mathrm{TC2}) for Γ\Gamma implies that XX is projective. By Lemma 2.1, MM is projective. ∎

The three-fold extension gives the corresponding implication for the first Tachikawa conjecture.

Theorem 3.6.

Let AA be an algebra and M∈mod⁡AM\in\operatorname{mod}A satisfy

ExtAi⁡(M,M⊕A)=0(i>0).\Ext_{A}^{i}(M,M\oplus A)=0\qquad(i>0).

Set Γ=T3​(A)\Gamma=T_{3}(A), X=M⊗Ae1​ΓX=M\otimes_{A}e_{1}\Gamma and

BM=EndΓ⁡(Γ⊕X).B_{M}=\End_{\Gamma}(\Gamma\oplus X).

Then domdim⁡BM=∞\domdim B_{M}=\infty and ExtBMi⁡(D​BM,BM)=0\Ext_{B_{M}}^{i}(DB_{M},B_{M})=0 for every i>0i>0. If BMB_{M} satisfies (TC1)(\mathrm{TC1}), then MM is projective. Consequently, global (TC1)(\mathrm{TC1}) implies global (ARC)(\mathrm{ARC}).

Proof.

By Lemma 3.2, Γ\Gamma is selfinjective. Proposition 3.4 gives

ExtΓi⁡(X,X)=ExtΓi⁡(νΓ​X,X)=0(i>0).\Ext_{\Gamma}^{i}(X,X)=\Ext_{\Gamma}^{i}(\nu_{\Gamma}X,X)=0\qquad(i>0).

Put V=Γ⊕XV=\Gamma\oplus X. The mixed summands with Γ\Gamma in ExtΓi⁡(V,V)\Ext_{\Gamma}^{i}(V,V) vanish because Γ\Gamma is projective and injective. Similarly, in ExtΓi⁡(νΓ​V,V)\Ext_{\Gamma}^{i}(\nu_{\Gamma}V,V) the summands with νΓ​Γ=D​Γ\nu_{\Gamma}\Gamma=D\Gamma in the first variable vanish because D​ΓD\Gamma is projective, and the summands with Γ\Gamma in the second variable vanish because Γ\Gamma is injective. Hence

ExtΓi⁡(V,V)=ExtΓi⁡(νΓ​V,V)=0(i>0).\Ext_{\Gamma}^{i}(V,V)=\Ext_{\Gamma}^{i}(\nu_{\Gamma}V,V)=0\qquad(i>0).

Proposition 2.3 now gives

ExtBMi⁡(D​BM,BM)≅ExtΓi⁡(νΓ​V,V)=0(i>0).\Ext_{B_{M}}^{i}(DB_{M},B_{M})\cong\Ext_{\Gamma}^{i}(\nu_{\Gamma}V,V)=0\qquad(i>0).

Since Γ\Gamma is selfinjective, VV is a generator-cogenerator, and the last assertion of Proposition 2.3 also gives domdim⁡BM=∞\domdim B_{M}=\infty. If BMB_{M} satisfies (TC1)(\mathrm{TC1}), then it is selfinjective. Lemma 2.4, applied to the generator-cogenerator VV over Γ\Gamma, implies that VV is projective. Therefore XX is projective. Finally, F1F_{1} reflects projectivity by Lemma 2.1, so MM is projective. ∎

We give now the proof of our first main theorem:

Theorem 3.7.

Fix a commutative artinian ring RR. The following conjectures are globally equivalent for Artin RR-algebras:

  1. (1)

    the Auslander–Reiten conjecture;

  2. (2)

    the generalised Nakayama conjecture;

  3. (3)

    the Nakayama conjecture;

  4. (4)

    the first Tachikawa conjecture;

  5. (5)

    the second Tachikawa conjecture.

Proof.

That (1) implies (2), (2) implies (3) and (3) implies (4) and (5) is well known, see for example [Yam96, Theorem 3.4.3]. In theorem 3.5 we proved that (5) implies (1) and in theorem 3.6 we proved that (4) implies (1) and thus all equivalences are proven.

∎

4. Tilting equivalences and the Chen–Xi conjecture

In this section algebras are finite dimensional over a fixed field KK, and D=HomK⁡(−,K)D=\Hom_{K}(-,K).

A Morita algebra is an algebra of the form EndS⁡(V)\End_{S}(V), where SS is selfinjective and VV is a generator-cogenerator; see [KY13]. A tilting module UAU_{A} has finite projective dimension n=pdimA⁡Un=\pdim_{A}U, satisfies ExtAi⁡(U,U)=0\Ext_{A}^{i}(U,U)=0 for all i>0i>0, and admits an exact sequence

0⟶A⟶U0⟶⋯⟶Un⟶0,Uj∈add⁡U.0\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow U_{0}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow U_{n}\longrightarrow 0,\qquad U_{j}\in\add U.

We write Db​(mod⁡A)\mathrm{D}^{\mathrm{b}}(\operatorname{mod}A) for the bounded derived category. For background on derived categories and tilting theory, see Krause [Kra22] and Zimmermann [Zim14]. For a tilting module UAU_{A}, put B=EndA⁡(U)B=\End_{A}(U), so UAB{}_{B}U_{A} is a bimodule. The tilting theorem gives quasi-inverse equivalences

𝐑HomA(U,−):Db(modA)⟶Db(modB),−⊗B𝐋U:Db(modB)⟶Db(modA).\mathbf{R}\Hom_{A}(U,-):\mathrm{D}^{\mathrm{b}}(\operatorname{mod}A)\longrightarrow\mathrm{D}^{\mathrm{b}}(\operatorname{mod}B),\qquad-\otimes_{B}^{\mathbf{L}}U:\mathrm{D}^{\mathrm{b}}(\operatorname{mod}B)\longrightarrow\mathrm{D}^{\mathrm{b}}(\operatorname{mod}A).

We recall the uniqueness part of the Morita–Tachikawa correspondence needed below; see [Mue68, Theorem 2 and the following remark, p. 401] and [Cru22, Theorem 2]. Every algebra AA with domdim⁡A≥2\domdim A\geq 2 has a presentation A≅EndS⁡(V)A\cong\End_{S}(V) with VV a generator-cogenerator, and SS is determined up to Morita equivalence. Moreover, Müller’s formula [Mue68, Lemma 3, pp. 401–402] gives

(4.1) domdim⁡EndS⁡(V)=1+inf{i≥1:ExtSi⁡(V,V)≠0},inf∅=∞.\domdim\End_{S}(V)=1+\inf\{i\geq 1:\Ext_{S}^{i}(V,V)\neq 0\},\qquad\inf\varnothing=\infty.

We also note that domdim⁡A=domdim⁡Aop\domdim A=\domdim A^{\mathrm{op}} [Mue68, Theorem 4, pp. 402–403]. For a module NN, write ΩA−1​N\Omega_{A}^{-1}N for the cokernel of its embedding into an injective envelope. The following construction is the first canonical tilting module considered in [CX16]. For the convenience of the reader we give the elementary proof.

Lemma 4.1.

Suppose domdim⁡A≥1\domdim A\geq 1, denote by I=I0​(A)I=I^{0}(A) the injective envelope of AA and C=ΩA−1​AC=\Omega_{A}^{-1}A. Then U=I⊕CU=I\oplus C is a tilting module of projective dimension at most one. If AA is not selfinjective, its projective dimension is one.

Proof.

The defining exact sequence

0⟶A⟶I⟶C⟶00\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow I\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow 0

has II projective, so pdimA⁡C≤1\pdim_{A}C\leq 1. Injectivity of II gives ExtA1⁡(C,I)=0\Ext_{A}^{1}(C,I)=0. We have ExtA1⁡(C,C)≅ExtA1⁡(C,Ω−1​(A))≅ExtA2⁡(C,A)=0\Ext_{A}^{1}(C,C)\cong\Ext_{A}^{1}(C,\Omega^{-1}(A))\cong\Ext_{A}^{2}(C,A)=0. Projectivity of II and pdimA⁡C≤1\pdim_{A}C\leq 1 now imply ExtAi⁡(U,U)=0\Ext_{A}^{i}(U,U)=0 for all i>0i>0. The displayed sequence has its last two terms in add⁡U\add U, and hence supplies the required tilting coresolution. If pdimA⁡U=0\pdim_{A}U=0, then CC is projective, the sequence splits, and AA is a direct summand of the injective module II. Thus AA is selfinjective. Conversely, when AA is selfinjective, I=AI=A, C=0C=0, and U=AU=A is a tilting module of projective dimension zero. ∎

We use the following consequences of Chen and Xi’s results.

Proposition 4.2 (Chen–Xi).
  1. (1)

    If domdim⁡A≥2\domdim A\geq 2 and I=I0​(A)I=I^{0}(A), then AA is a Morita algebra if and only if add⁡I=add⁡νA​I\add I=\add\nu_{A}I.

  2. (2)

    If domdim⁡A≥2\domdim A\geq 2 and AA is not a Morita algebra, the canonical tilting module of Lemma 4.1 satisfies domdim⁡EndA⁡(I⊕ΩA−1​A)≤1\domdim\End_{A}(I\oplus\Omega_{A}^{-1}A)\leq 1.

Proof.

Part (1) follows from [CX16, Lemmas 3.4(1) and 3.8]. Part (2) is [CX16, Proposition 4.17(1)] for the first canonical tilting module. ∎

As before, we denote by NC⁡(A)\mathrm{NC}(A) the statement that the Nakayama conjecture is true for the algebra AA, that is domdim⁡A=∞\domdim A=\infty implies that AA is selfinjective.

Theorem 4.3.

The following statements, quantified over all finite dimensional KK-algebras, are equivalent.

  1. (A)

    For every tilting module UAU_{A}, with B=EndA⁡(U)B=\End_{A}(U), the statements NC⁡(A)\mathrm{NC}(A) and NC⁡(B)\mathrm{NC}(B) are equivalent.

  2. (B)

    Every algebra of infinite dominant dimension is a Morita algebra.

  3. (C)

    The first Tachikawa conjecture holds for every algebra.

Proof.

First assume (C). If domdim⁡A=∞\domdim A=\infty, choose A≅EndS⁡(V)A\cong\End_{S}(V) by Morita–Tachikawa with a generator-cogenerator SS-module VV. Formula (4.1) gives ExtSi⁡(V,V)=0\Ext_{S}^{i}(V,V)=0 for every i>0i>0. Since S,D​S∈add⁡VS,DS\in\add V, it follows that ExtSi⁡(D​S,S)=0\Ext_{S}^{i}(DS,S)=0 for every i>0i>0. By the first Tachikawa conjecture, SS is selfinjective. Hence AA is Morita, proving (B).

Conversely, assume (B) and suppose ExtSi⁡(D​S,S)=0\Ext_{S}^{i}(DS,S)=0 for every i>0i>0. Put V=S⊕D​SV=S\oplus DS. Projectivity of SS, injectivity of D​SDS, and the assumed vanishing give ExtSi⁡(V,V)=0\Ext_{S}^{i}(V,V)=0 for all i>0i>0. Thus A=EndS⁡(V)A=\End_{S}(V) has infinite dominant dimension by (4.1), and is Morita by (B). It therefore also has a presentation as the endomorphism algebra of a generator-cogenerator over a selfinjective algebra. Uniqueness in the Morita–Tachikawa correspondence makes SS Morita equivalent to that selfinjective algebra. Since selfinjectivity is Morita invariant, SS is selfinjective. This proves (C).

Next assume (A), and let domdim⁡A=∞\domdim A=\infty. If AA is selfinjective it is already a Morita algebra, using the presentation A≅EndA⁡(A)A\cong\End_{A}(A). Otherwise, the canonical tilting module U=I0​(A)⊕ΩA−1​AU=I^{0}(A)\oplus\Omega_{A}^{-1}A is of projective dimension one. If AA were not Morita, Proposition 4.2(2) would give domdim⁡EndA⁡(U)≤1\domdim\End_{A}(U)\leq 1. Hence NC⁡(EndA⁡(U))\mathrm{NC}(\End_{A}(U)) holds vacuously, and (A) gives NC⁡(A)\mathrm{NC}(A). As domdim⁡A=∞\domdim A=\infty, the algebra AA is then selfinjective, and therefore Morita, a contradiction. This proves (B).

Finally assume (B). We have proved that this implies (C). Theorem 1.1, applied with R=KR=K, then gives the Nakayama conjecture for all finite dimensional KK-algebras. Thus, for any tilting module UAU_{A} and B=EndA⁡(U)B=\End_{A}(U), both NC⁡(A)\mathrm{NC}(A) and NC⁡(B)\mathrm{NC}(B) are true. In particular they are equivalent, proving (A). ∎

Chen and Xi formulated their conjecture for finite dimensional algebras over a field [CX16, §5.2, conjecture (1)]; see also [Xi18, Conjecture 6.5]. More precisely, their assertion is

(4.2) Db(modA)≃Db(modB)⟹(domdimA<∞⟺domdimB<∞).\mathrm{D}^{\mathrm{b}}(\operatorname{mod}A)\simeq\mathrm{D}^{\mathrm{b}}(\operatorname{mod}B)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\bigl(\domdim A<\infty\Longleftrightarrow\domdim B<\infty\bigr).

We can now prove Theorem 1.3 in the following expanded form.

Theorem 4.4.

For finite dimensional algebras over a fixed field KK, the following statements are equivalent:

  1. (1)

    the Nakayama conjecture holds for every algebra;

  2. (2)

    the first Tachikawa conjecture holds for every algebra;

  3. (3)

    the Nakayama implication NC⁡(A)\mathrm{NC}(A) is invariant under derived equivalences;

  4. (4)

    the Chen–Xi conjecture (4.2) holds.

Each is also equivalent to the conditions of Theorem 4.3.

Proof.

The equivalence of (1) and (2) is part of Theorem 1.1, with R=KR=K. Statement (1) implies (3) immediately. Statement (3) implies condition (A) of Theorem 4.3, since tilting equivalences are derived equivalences; that theorem then gives (2).

Under (1), an algebra has infinite dominant dimension exactly when it is selfinjective. Since selfinjectivity is preserved under derived equivalences by [XZ25, Corollary 5.3], this proves (4). Conversely, assume (4). If an algebra AA of infinite dominant dimension were not Morita, the canonical tilting module as in the proof of Theorem 4.3 would produce a derived equivalent algebra of dominant dimension at most one. This contradicts (4). Thus condition (B) of that theorem holds, giving (2), and hence (1). ∎

As a final remark, we note that we worked in this section with algebras over field instead of general Artin algebras, since we used that being selfinjective is closed under derived equivalences, which is to our knowledge only established for algebras over fields in [XZ25]. The conjecture of Chen-Xi is stated for algebras over fields.
